Privacy Policy

Effective September 24, 2026 · Version 2.6

The short version. Remvoll runs on your device. We do not operate analytics servers, advertising SDKs, or tracking pixels. Your settings, presets, sleep history and any morning note are encrypted on your device, background photos you add stay on your device too, and none of it is transmitted to us. There are no accounts, so there is no profile of you anywhere. Microphone features are strictly opt-in, process sound locally as numbers only, and store nothing. The detailed disclosures below are provided so the policy is complete and durable as the product grows.

1. Scope and who we are

This Privacy Policy explains how Remvoll ("Remvoll," "we," "us," "our") handles information in connection with the Remvoll application, its websites, and related services (the "Service"). It applies to Users of the Service and forms part of our Terms of Service. Remvoll is published by an individual developer, not a company; the developer's name is shown as the seller on Remvoll's App Store page. For the purposes of the EU/UK General Data Protection Regulation, the processing described here happens on your device; to the extent any of it is attributed to us, the developer is the controller. Contact: privacy@remvoll.com. Because this build makes no network calls carrying personal data, there is currently nothing held on our side to access, correct, or delete.

2. Our privacy principles

  • Local-first by architecture. Personal data is processed and stored on your device, not on our servers.
  • Data minimization. We collect only what a feature genuinely needs to function.
  • No surveillance business model. We do not sell or share personal information, run behavioral advertising, or profile you.
  • Security by design. Sensitive data is encrypted at rest; credentials are never stored in plaintext.
  • Transparency. If we ever introduce a network feature, we will update this policy first and describe exactly what changes.

3. Information we collect and process

On our servers: none. This build has no server-side account database, no telemetry endpoint, and no third-party analytics. The following categories are created and stored locally on your device, in the app's own container, encrypted under a key held in the iOS Keychain:

  • Preferences. Theme, volume, breathing pace, timer, listening mode, alarm settings and effects toggles, so the app remembers how you like it. Legal basis where GDPR applies: performance of a contract.
  • Presets. The sound mixes you build and name. Performance of a contract.
  • Sleep history. Playback session summaries: times, duration, sounds used, breathing setting and playback disturbances, shown on your Sleep Score page. Performance of a contract; consent where required.
  • Health readings, if you allow them. Sleep and heart-rate data read from Apple Health — recorded there by your Apple Watch or by another device or app that writes sleep data to Health. Used for two things only: choosing the moment Smart Wake rings, and working out last night's Sleep Score (how long you were asleep and how much of the night you stayed asleep). Read-only, never written back, never retained as samples, and never sent anywhere; the Sleep Score's figures are worked out again from Health each time you open the page rather than stored. Explicit consent, which you grant in the iOS Health prompt and can revoke there at any time. Remvoll also keeps a learned sleep-timing pattern derived from those nights: how long you usually take to fall asleep, your usual bedtime, how long each of your sleep cycles tends to run and how that changes across a night, and how often each sleep stage has appeared at each point after you fell asleep. It contains no Health samples, no timestamps of individual readings and nothing about any specific night — only running statistics. It is stored encrypted on your device, is never transmitted, and exists so Smart Wake can still aim for a light moment on nights you do not wear a Watch. Erasing your sleep history erases it too.
  • Microphone loudness, if you turn it on. A single number every few seconds while sound is playing. No audio is recorded, retained or transmitted; each reading is discarded once used. Explicit consent.
  • A morning note, if you make one. A short voice recording you make deliberately from the alarm screen, or text you type, to be shown to you the next morning. If your device supports offline dictation, a recording is also written out as text, on the device only. Stored encrypted on your device and never uploaded; exactly one exists at a time, and making another replaces it. Consent.
  • Background photos, if you add one. When you pick a picture, iOS hands Remvoll only that picture — the app has no access to the rest of your photo library. The part you frame is saved in the app's storage with a small thumbnail, along with a reduced-size copy of the whole picture and the framing you chose, so you can double-tap it later to re-frame it. These stay inside the app's sandbox under iOS file protection, but not in Remvoll's own encrypted store, and they are included in backups of your iPhone like other app files. Never transmitted. Remove one by touching and holding it in Settings › Background, which deletes all of its copies. Performance of a contract.
  • Reminders, if you turn them on. A reminder two days before a free trial ends, and a daily wind-down reminder at a time you choose. Both are local notifications: iOS holds them on your device and shows them, and nothing is sent to us. The wind-down time is stored with your settings. Turn them off in Settings › Bedtime or in iOS Settings › Notifications. Consent.
  • Siri and Shortcuts, if you use them. Remvoll offers "Start sleep" and "Stop" actions to Siri, the Shortcuts app and automations such as one that runs when Sleep Focus turns on. Apple runs those actions; Remvoll receives only the action itself, never your voice or anything about your automations.

There are no account identifiers, no email address, no password, no credentials and no membership record, because the app has no accounts and Apple holds the subscription.

Sleep history describes application playback, not your body. Remvoll has no sensors of its own. Where you have granted Health access, it reads sleep and heart-rate samples that your Watch, another tracker, or iOS already recorded, and uses them to time an alarm and to work out the Sleep Score. The samples themselves are not retained; what is kept is a statistical summary of your sleep TIMING, described above, which stays on the device.

4. Information we do NOT collect

  • No audio recordings, except a morning note you choose to record.
  • No precise or approximate location, contacts, calendar, or files, and no access to your photo library — only the single picture you pick, if you add a background.
  • No health data of any kind unless you explicitly allow it in the iOS Health prompt, and then only sleep and heart rate, read-only, kept on the device and used solely for Smart Wake and the Sleep Score — together with the on-device learned timing pattern derived from them, which never leaves the device and is erased with your sleep history.
  • No medical diagnosis or health inference. The Sleep Score summarizes what was recorded about a night; it is not a health assessment.
  • No advertising identifiers, device fingerprints, or cross-app/cross-site tracking.
  • No record of App Store ratings. Remvoll may occasionally show Apple's own rating prompt; Apple shows it and handles anything you submit, and Remvoll never learns whether it appeared or what you chose.
  • No behavioral analytics, heatmaps, or session-replay.
  • We do not knowingly collect data from children under the applicable minimum age.

4A. Blocking apps (Screen Time)

Remvoll can stop chosen apps from opening — on a schedule you set, or for a few minutes after your alarm rings. This uses Apple's Screen Time frameworks (Family Controls, Managed Settings and Device Activity) and is opt-in: it does nothing until you grant Screen Time access at an operating-system prompt, and it stops entirely if you withdraw that access in iOS Settings.

What Remvoll can and cannot see. When you choose which apps to block, iOS presents its own picker and returns sealed tokens, not names. This is a property of Apple's framework, not a promise about our restraint: the app is structurally incapable of learning which apps you selected. Remvoll does not receive, and cannot derive, the names of your apps, how long you use them, how often you open them, or whether a block was ever hit. No app-usage data of any kind is collected, stored or transmitted.

What is stored, and where. The sealed tokens, your schedules, and a note of which block is currently in force are written to a shared App Group container on your device so that the Remvoll Blocking helper — a small background extension — can read them. That container is not encrypted by us, because an extension cannot reach our encrypted store; it holds no names, no usage, and nothing that identifies you. None of it leaves the device.

Why there is a background helper. A block, once applied, is a system-wide setting that outlives the app. Something has to run at the far end of a block to lift it even if you never reopen Remvoll, and iOS provides exactly one mechanism for that. The helper exists for that single purpose: it turns a block on when its window starts and off when the window ends. It has no network access.

Limits you should know. iOS never permits an app to block Phone, Messages or Settings, and Remvoll could not do so if it wanted to. Any block can be ended immediately from the Block apps screen, and a block whose time has passed is cleared automatically by both the helper and the app.

5. Microphone

  • Off by default. The microphone has three modes: Off, Count noise, and Auto volume. Off uses no microphone.
  • Opt-in only. Count noise and Auto volume each need an in-app choice and the iOS microphone permission, and run only while sound is playing.
  • Local, ephemeral, numeric. When on, the microphone feeds a loudness meter that produces one number every few seconds. Count noise uses it to count noisy moments for your Sleep Score page; Auto volume uses it to raise playback volume a little when the room gets louder. The audio is never encoded, recorded, kept beyond the meter window, transmitted, or stored.
  • Immediate release. Turning the mode off or stopping playback releases the microphone at once.
  • Morning notes are separate. Recording a morning note is its own deliberate action, described in Section 3.

6. How we use information

Locally-stored information is used to: provide and personalise the Service; save and apply your presets and preferences; show your Sleep Score and sleep history; manage your trial and membership state; secure the Service against unauthorized access; and comply with legal obligations. We do not use your information for advertising, profiling, or automated decision-making producing legal or similarly significant effects.

7. Legal bases for processing (EEA/UK)

Where the GDPR or UK GDPR applies to any processing, we rely on: (a) performance of a contract, to provide features you request; (b) our legitimate interests, for security and to operate and improve the Service in ways that do not override your rights; (c) your consent, for optional features such as the microphone modes and morning notes, and your explicit consent under Article 9(2)(a) GDPR for the health data read from Apple Health, which is special-category data — you may withdraw either at any time; and (d) compliance with legal obligations where applicable. Where processing occurs solely on your device under your control, you are the party determining that processing.

8. Sign-in providers

There are none, because there is no sign-in. Remvoll does not offer Sign in with Apple, Sign in with Google, or any other federated identity, and does not ask for an email address. If that ever changes, this policy will be updated before it ships.

9. Payments

Subscriptions are sold and billed by Apple through the App Store. Payment details are given to Apple, never to us: Remvoll does not receive, see, or store a card number, billing address, or Apple Account identifier. What the app reads is Apple's own signed answer to "does this device have an active subscription", which it uses to decide what to unlock.

10. Sharing and disclosure

We do not sell your personal information and do not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising. Because this build stores nothing on our servers, we generally have nothing to disclose. If, at launch, limited processors are engaged (for example, an app store, a payment processor, or an identity provider), they will act under contractual confidentiality and data-protection obligations and only as necessary to provide their service. We may disclose information if required to do so by law, to respond to valid legal process, to enforce our Terms, or to protect the rights, property, or safety of Remvoll, our users, or the public — though, having no user data on servers in this build, there is typically nothing we could produce.

11. International transfers

Because data is stored on your device, it resides wherever your device is and is not transferred by us across borders. If future features involve any transfer of personal data internationally, we will implement appropriate safeguards (such as Standard Contractual Clauses) and describe them here.

12. Data retention

Sleep history keeps at most the most recent 400 sessions; older entries are discarded automatically. Health samples are not retained at all. Background photos, their reduced originals and framing stay until you remove them. Everything else persists until you erase it in the app or delete the app, which removes all of it at once. We hold no server-side copies to retain, so there is nothing on our side with a retention period.

13. Your rights and controls

You have robust, immediate control because your data lives on your device:

  • Access & portability: Settings › Export my data produces a complete JSON copy of what Remvoll stores.
  • Erasure: Settings › Erase sleep history deletes your sleep history and the learned sleep-timing pattern immediately and permanently. Deleting the app removes everything else it stored, including its encryption key, in one step.
  • Rectification: update your preferences directly in the app.
  • Restriction/objection & consent withdrawal: turn off optional features at any time — the microphone modes and reminders in Settings, Health access in the iOS Health app, and a background photo or morning note by removing it.

Depending on where you live, you may have additional rights under laws such as the GDPR/UK GDPR, the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended (CCPA/CPRA), and similar U.S. state laws. These include rights to know, access, correct, delete, and to non-discrimination for exercising your rights; we do not sell or "share" personal information as those terms are defined. The in-app controls satisfy these rights without needing to contact us. Where a verifiable request is nonetheless required, contact us at the address above; you may also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data-protection authority.

14. Children's privacy

The Service is not directed to children under 13 (or the higher applicable minimum age) and does not knowingly collect their personal data. The app contains no chat, social features, user-to-user content, or advertising. If you believe a child has provided personal data in a future networked feature, contact us and we will act promptly.

15. Security

On iOS, app data is held in the app's own sandboxed container with encryption at rest, and the key is stored in the iOS Keychain. Because there is no Remvoll account and no server, there is no password to steal and nothing to breach remotely. The honest limitation is the obvious one: anyone who can unlock your device can open the app and see what is in it. No method of storage is perfectly secure.

16. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control

The Service performs no tracking of any kind, so "Do Not Track" and "Global Privacy Control" signals have nothing to act upon; we honour them by design, because we simply do not track. NSPrivacyTracking is declared false in the app's privacy manifest and there are no tracking domains to declare.

17. Changes to this Policy

We may update this Policy to reflect changes in the Service or the law. Material changes — especially any that introduce network transmission of personal data — will be announced in-app before they take effect, and we will keep the local-first defaults. The "Effective" date above indicates the latest revision.

Privacy questions or requests: privacy@remvoll.com.
